prayerExcerpt.en-US: Go forth, my soul; why dost thou doubt? Nigh seventy years hast thou served God, and dost thou fear death?
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Sai, minha alma; por que duvidas? Por quase setenta anos serviste a Deus, e temes a morte?

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-22-mello.md, his last paragraph, his dying words; the chapter, shared with St. Mello (`mello`, batch 37), has no Reflection, so this card has no reflection (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Hilarion, half-length, an aged hermit of the fourth century: a rough shirt of undyed sackcloth and over it a small, worn cloak of brown skins (the one St. Antony gave him), bareheaded; in his hands a half-woven basket of rushes resting against his breast, his fingers still at the weaving. Behind him the sandy desert inland from Gaza: low dunes, a few date palms, a tiny, low cell of reeds and clay, hardly taller than a man, and far off a thin blue line of the Mediterranean under a pale evening sky. Gentle, humble and at peace; no skull, no scroll, no lettering.
cards.face: A Palestinian of about eighty, worn thin by fasting, with a dry, sun-browned olive complexion and a face whose PROFILE is CONVEX — a forehead that SLOPES BACK from a knotted brow, a LONG, gently CURVED nose that projects far forward, and a SMALL, RECEDING chin, so that the face seems drawn forward to a point at the nose; narrow temples, flat, lined cheeks, SMALL, almond-shaped, soft brown eyes under HEAVY, half-lowered lids and wispy grey brows, deep crow's-feet; thin, dry, rough-cut hair, BROWN streaked with grey, short about the ears; a long, thin, BROWN, rush-like beard, streaked with grey and divided into THREE narrow points, as the Painter's Manual has it; the gaze lowered, meek. Not the triangular, hooded anthony_abbot, the long-tapering, bald, wide-eyed paul_hermit, the small, chiselled, two-point-bearded simeon_stylites, the elfin john_egypt, the horse-like paphnutius, the diamond-shaped porphyry_gaza or the rounded-square macarius_alexandria.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual of Dionysius of Fourna (`consult/hermeneia-ocr.txt`, 21 October) gives him as an old man with a brown, rush-like beard divided into three points, which English Wikipedia repeats for his icons; the sackcloth, the cloak of skins from St. Antony, the rush baskets and the tiny cell are from St. Jerome's Life of St. Hilarion (NPNF tr., `jerome-hilarion.txt`).

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Take care to meditate upon the four last things, and to live in holy fear.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Cuida de meditar sobre as quatro últimas coisas e de viver no santo temor.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-23-theodoret.md Reflection, second sentence (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Theodoret, half-length, a priest of Antioch in the year 362: a long white linen tunic and over it a plain, dark-red paenula falling in soft folds, bareheaded; he holds a martyr's palm in his right hand and presses a small silver chalice, one of the church's sacred vessels he kept, against his breast with his left. Behind him Antioch on the Orontes: colonnaded streets and tiled roofs climbing the slope of Mount Silpius, a closed church door in the foreground street, a warm late-afternoon light. Steadfast, grave and fearless; no ropes, no wounds, no lettering.
cards.face: A Syrian of Antioch of about forty-five with a warm, olive complexion and a face shaped like a BELL — NARROW at the temples and the low forehead, WIDENING down to a BROAD, ANGULAR jaw with marked corners; a strong nose with a distinct BUMP on the bridge and a straight, slightly down-turned tip, deep-set, dark, steady eyes under thick black brows ARCHED HIGH at their middle, flat cheeks, a firm mouth with a FULL lower lip; short, thick, black curly hair cropped close to the skull; a SHORT, dense, curly black beard that follows the wide jaw closely; the look direct and unafraid. Not the short, domed-browed lucian_antioch, the square-jawed, full-cheeked Cosmas of cosmas_damian, the long-headed, joined-browed romanus_ostiarius or the broad-browed, clean-shaven eusebius_rome.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The face is a strong Syrian priest's, faithful to the book's account of his bold answer to Count Julian; that he kept the church's sacred vessels is from Wikipedia (after Butler), and the book's engraving shows him before the tribunal.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: "Be mindful of them that have rule over you, who have spoken to you the word of God, whose faith follow, considering the end."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Lembrai-vos dos vossos guias, que vos anunciaram a palavra de Deus; e, considerando o fim da sua vida, imitai-lhes a fé."

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-24-magloire.md Reflection, the whole of it (Hebrews 13:7) (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Magloire, half-length, an aged Breton bishop and abbot of the sixth century: a plain dark monastic cowl with its hood fallen back, and over it a simple white pallium-like stole of a Celtic bishop; a plain wooden crozier with a curved head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing. Behind him a small, rocky island in the Channel with steep green cliffs, a cluster of small stone cells and a tiny chapel on its top, a grey-blue sea with white surf and a single fishing boat, a soft, bright, cloudy sky. Venerable, kindly and serene; no mitre, no lettering.
cards.face: A Briton of about seventy-five, spare and upright, with a fair, wind-reddened complexion and a TALL, NARROW face that is LONGEST between the eyes and the mouth — a high, BALD, smooth DOME with a fringe of white hair at the back, a LONG, THIN, straight nose that ENDS in a slightly DROOPING tip, WIDE-SET, clear, light-blue eyes under THIN, level white brows, HIGH, NARROW cheekbones with flat planes below, a LONG upper lip and a small mouth, LARGE ears; a long, STRAIGHT, silver-white beard that TAPERS to a single narrow point on the breast; the gaze calm and benevolent, toward us. Not the dish-profiled, snub-nosed, wavy-bearded mello, the heavy-browed, broad david_wales, the shield-shaped paternus_avranches, the trapezoid, broad-bearded hilary, the long, symmetrical remigius, or the round, bald, flat-featured zephyrinus.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The painting on English Wikipedia's page shows a tall old bishop with a high bald forehead and a long white beard, which the card keeps; the book has him resign his see at seventy and govern sixty monks on an island (Jersey in the book, Sark in Wikipedia and the Martyrology's tradition), so the island is left unnamed.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Of how many may it be said that "they labor in vain," since God is not the end and purpose that inspires the labor?
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: De quantos se pode dizer que "trabalham em vão", visto que Deus não é o fim e o propósito que inspira o trabalho?

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-25-sts-crispin-and-crispinian.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: Sts. Crispin and Crispinian, side by side, half-length, two brothers of a noble Roman family working as shoemakers in Gallo-Roman Soissons about 285: plain belted tunics of undyed wool with leather aprons, sleeves pushed up; Crispin (left) holds a finished leather sandal and a martyr's palm, Crispinian (right) a shoemaker's awl and a wooden last with a palm resting in the crook of his arm. Behind them their small workshop open to the street: a work bench with leather, thread and a hanging row of sandals, an oil lamp burning for the night's work, and through the doorway the tiled roofs of Roman Soissons and a few townspeople listening. Two brothers who are clearly different men; humble, cheerful, devout; no swords, no millstones, no lettering.
cards.face: Two brothers who must read as different men, NOT twins. CRISPIN (left), the elder, about forty, with a ruddy olive complexion and a WIDE, SHORT, FLAT face — a broad, low forehead under a STRAIGHT, low hairline of short, thick black hair, WIDE, FLAT cheekbones, a SHORT, BROAD nose with a low bridge, small, bright, dark eyes creased by a ready smile under thick, straight black brows, a WIDE mouth, a strong, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN with a dark shadow on the jaw, a thick neck. CRISPINIAN (right), about thirty, paler, with a TRIANGULAR face — BROAD temples and a high, smooth forehead tapering past lean cheeks to a NARROW, POINTED chin; a thin, straight nose, LARGE, grey-green eyes set wide, fine, arched light-brown brows, a small, thoughtful mouth; soft, wavy, light-brown hair to the ears and a SPARSE, short light-brown beard only on the chin; the gaze earnest. Not the olive twins of cosmas_damian, nor the pairs john_paul_martyrs, faustinus_jovita or romanus_lupicinus.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The Kalkar statues (Wikipedia's lead image) make them two young, well-dressed men with shoemakers' tools; the card keeps the tools and palms, makes them different in age and build as brothers, not twins (the book says only 'brothers'), and sets them in the Soissons workshop of the book's engraving.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: The disciples of the apostles, by assiduous meditation on heavenly things, were so swallowed up in the life to come, that they seemed no longer inhabitants of this world.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Os discípulos dos apóstolos, pela assídua meditação nas coisas celestiais, estavam tão absortos na vida futura que pareciam já não ser habitantes deste mundo.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-26-evaristus.md Reflection, first sentence (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Evaristus, half-length, the bishop of Rome about the year 105 in the plain dress of his time: a long white tunic and a wide, cream woollen pallium (the Greek mantle) draped over the left shoulder, bareheaded, no tiara, no mitre; he holds a small scroll of the Scriptures in his left hand and lifts his right a little as if assigning a task. Behind him, under a clear Roman sky, the Vatican hill with its cypresses and tombs, where St. Peter lies buried, and beyond the Tiber the roofs of Trajan's Rome. Grave, recollected and fatherly; no lettering.
cards.face: A Greek of Jewish family from Bethlehem, about sixty-five, with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a face DOMINATED by a LARGE, STRONGLY ARCHED, high-bridged nose — a LOW forehead under a WIDOW'S PEAK of thick, WAVY grey hair brushed back and still full, HOODED, dark-brown eyes that SLANT DOWN at the outer corners under thick, level, black-and-grey brows, HIGH cheekbones over LEAN cheeks, a deep groove above a thin-lipped mouth, a NARROW chin; a MEDIUM, black-and-grey beard cut SQUARE across the bottom; the gaze inward and grave. Not the round, bald, crisp-bearded mark_pope, the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the soft, heart-shaped soter, the hexagonal linus, the bony, two-pointed cletus, the diamond-faced clement_i or the long, narrow sylvester.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; the Sistine Chapel portrait (Wikipedia's lead image) and the medallion of St. Paul Outside the Walls are late and conventional. The card takes the Liber Pontificalis's Greek of Jewish family from Bethlehem (via Wikipedia) and gives him a Levantine face, bareheaded in first-century dress, on the Vatican hill, where the book says he was buried near St. Peter.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: "The soul that journeys in the light and the truths of the Faith is safe against all error."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "A alma que caminha na luz e nas verdades da Fé está a salvo de todo erro."

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-27-frumentius.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Frumentius, half-length, a bishop of the fourth century: a white linen tunic, a plain saffron-gold paenula, and a white woollen pallium marked with dark crosses around his shoulders, bareheaded; he holds a Gospel book bound in plain leather with a small cross on it against his breast and raises his right hand in blessing. Behind him the highland city of Axum: tall, carved granite stelae standing among acacia trees, stone buildings, green terraced hills and a few Aksumite people in white cotton robes, small in the distance, under a high, clear sky. Kindly, wise and steadfast; no lettering.
cards.face: A Phoenician of Tyre of about fifty-five with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a WIDE, LOW, FLAT-CHEEKED face — a BROAD, low forehead, WIDE, flat cheek planes and a WIDE jaw, THICK, black brows ARCHED high and full, LARGE, dark, slightly PROMINENT eyes with a kind, direct look, a nose with a strong, gentle CURVE and a FLESHY, rounded tip, a FULL, wide mouth; thick, wavy black hair touched with grey at the temples, falling to the neck; a full, thick black beard, rounded at the bottom; the gaze warm and steady. Not the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the round, soft severianus_scythopolis, the short, domed lucian_antioch or the Copts pachomius and macarius_alexandria.
cards.basis: The modern icon on English Wikipedia's page shows a dark-haired, full-bearded bishop; no likeness survives, so the card keeps the icon's colouring on a broad Levantine face, the boy of Tyre grown into the bishop the book says St. Athanasius ordained. Axum and its court are from the book and from Rufinus via Wikipedia.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: God never fails those who trust in Him; He guides them through darkness and through trials secretly and surely to their end, and in the evening time there is light.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Deus nunca falha àqueles que n'Ele confiam; Ele os guia através das trevas e das provações, secreta e seguramente, ao seu fim, e na hora da tarde haverá luz.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-29-narcissus.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Narcissus, half-length, the bishop of Jerusalem about the year 200, very old and a little stooped: a white tunic and a plain, deep-blue paenula with a white woollen pallium marked with dark crosses, bareheaded; he holds up in both hands a small clay oil lamp burning with a clear flame, the lamp of the Paschal vigil whose water he turned to oil. Behind him the hills of Jerusalem at dusk, the city's pale stone walls and roofs, a few olive trees and the first stars in a deep-blue evening sky. Serene, patient and full of trust; no mitre, no lettering.
cards.face: A man of great age, well past a hundred, with a soft, pale, parchment-fine complexion and a SMALL, ROUND, SHRUNKEN face in which the mouth has FALLEN IN, bringing a small, HOOKED nose and a small, forward-CURVING chin close together (a gentle 'nutcracker' profile) — a round, BALD crown with a few wisps of fine white hair at the sides, small, soft, watery-blue eyes deep in folds of skin, puffed, softly drooping lids, sparse, long white brows, rounded, sunken cheeks; a SHORT, SPARSE, soft white beard that shows the chin's shape beneath; the gaze mild and trusting, the lips in a faint smile. Not the long, hatchet-faced simeon_jerusalem, the rosy, heart-shaped, full-haired polycarp, the long, tapering paul_hermit, the broad, flat-planed theodosius_cenobiarch or the round, flat-featured, long-bearded zephyrinus.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The book and the Martyrology make him bishop in extreme old age (the Martyrology: 116 years at his death), so the card paints a very old man; the lamp is the book's Easter miracle of water turned to oil, told also by Eusebius (via Wikipedia).

prayerExcerpt.en-US: "We are ready to die rather than to transgress the laws of God!" exclaimed one of the Machabees. This sentiment should ever be that of a Christian in presence of temptation.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Estamos prontos a morrer antes que transgredir as leis de Deus!" exclamou um dos Macabeus. Este sentimento deve ser sempre o de um cristão em presença da tentação.

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-30-marcellus-the-centurion.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Marcellus the Centurion, half-length, a Roman centurion of the year 298: a red woollen tunic and a scale-mail cuirass, a red cloak pinned at the shoulder, bareheaded; he has UNBUCKLED his military belt and holds it out with his sword in its scabbard in his right hand, as if laying them down, while his left hand rests on his breast; his vine staff lies at his feet. Behind him the legion's camp on the emperor's birthday: rows of leather tents, the standards with their eagles and garlands, a smoking altar and small, distant soldiers feasting, under a hot, hazy sky with dry hills. Resolute, calm and clear-eyed; no wounds, no executioner, no lettering.
cards.face: A veteran of about forty-five with a sun-browned, ruddy olive complexion and a ROUND, SHORT face as wide as it is long on a THICK neck — a broad, rounded forehead, FULL, firm, ROUNDED cheeks, a SHORT, slightly UPTURNED nose, ROUND, light-brown eyes, frank and steady, under STRAIGHT, thick brown brows, a WIDE, good-humoured mouth, a round chin with a DIMPLE; brown hair going grey, cut very short in the soldier's fashion; a SHORT, close-trimmed grizzled beard; the look firm and open. Not the angular, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, the long-headed, joined-browed romanus_ostiarius, the square, broken-nosed Tarachus of tarachus_companions, the dark, long-oval Maurice of theban_legion, or george and sebastian.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. The book and the Martyrology tell of his throwing down his belt and arms before the standards on the emperor's feast; the book's engraving shows him among soldiers and tents with his arms on the ground. The round, open face is a veteran's, chosen to stand apart from the batch's other soldiers.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Let us bear in mind that the ills of this life are not worthy to be compared to the glory "God has reserved for those who love Him."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Tenhamos em mente que os males desta vida não são dignos de ser comparados com a glória que "Deus reservou para aqueles que O amam".

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/oct-31-quintin.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Quintin, half-length, a young Roman of senatorial family preaching in Gaul about 287: a white tunic with the broad purple stripe of a senator's son and a white toga-like pallium draped over the shoulder, bareheaded; a martyr's palm in his right hand, his left open toward the listeners. Behind him Roman Amiens on the Somme: a wooden bridge over the river, reed-marshes and poplars, tiled roofs and a small forum, a few Gallic townspeople in hooded cloaks listening, under a soft, grey-blue northern sky. Young, ardent and gentle; no nails, no chains, no wounds, no lettering.
cards.face: A Roman patrician of about thirty, CLEAN-SHAVEN, fair-skinned with a light flush, with a LONG, RECTANGULAR face and a STRONG, FLAT-BOTTOMED jaw as wide as the cheekbones — a high, broad forehead, a Roman nose with a HIGH bridge and a slight HOOK, DEEP-SET, grey-green eyes under straight, fair-brown brows, flat cheeks, a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth, a long neck; short, TIGHT, close-cropped fair curls; the gaze eager and bright. Not the smooth-oval, fringe-haired alexander, the round-faced boy pancras, the angular, cleft-chinned victor_marseilles, the long-headed romanus_ostiarius, or the heart-shaped youngest of forty_martyrs_sebaste.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. Pontormo's painting (Wikipedia's lead image) makes him a young man; the card keeps his youth and senatorial rank from the book and the Martyrology ('senatore'), and puts him at Amiens, where the book has him preach and suffer.

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Our Lord said to St. Gertrude, "God accepts every soul you set free, as if you had redeemed him from captivity, and will reward you in a fitting time for the benefit you have conferred."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Nosso Senhor disse a Santa Gertrudes: "Deus aceita cada alma que libertas, como se a tivesses resgatado do cativeiro, e te recompensará no tempo devido pelo benefício que conferiste."

cards.excerptSource: content/books/pictorial-lives-of-saints/{en-US,pt-BR}/nov-02-malachi.md Reflection, the whole of it (Pictorial Lives, public domain)
cards.subject: St. Malachi, half-length, an Irish archbishop of about 1140: a white alb, a plain green chasuble of the twelfth century falling in wide, soft folds, a low white mitre; a simple crozier with a curled head in his left hand, his right raised in blessing. Behind him a green hill in Ireland with a small stone church, low stone walls and a churchyard with a few crosses, soft Irish light after rain. Grave, cheerful and gentle; no lettering.
cards.face: An Irishman of about fifty with a fair, fresh, lightly ruddy complexion and a smooth, UNLINED, OVAL face somewhat LONGER than wide — a high, ROUNDED forehead, a SHORT, straight nose with a slightly UPTURNED, neat tip, LARGE, clear, grey-blue eyes set WIDE apart, their lower lids lifted by a quiet smile, soft, arched brown brows, FIRM, smooth cheeks, a small, calm, closed mouth turned up at the corners, a SMALL, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; brown hair greying a little, cut short in a Roman round tonsure; the gaze grave but joyful. Not the broad, white-haired, Irish-tonsured columba, the long, flaxen finbarr, the heart-shaped fiaker, the square, snub-nosed gall, the big-boned columban, the long, handsome oswald_worcester, or the clean-shaven, beak-nosed wilfrid.
cards.basis: No likeness survives. St. Bernard's Life of St. Malachy (tr. Lawlor, 1920, `bernard-malachy.txt`) says that 'neither did sadness darken nor laughter turn to levity the joyousness of his countenance' and that even in death his brow was not wrinkled nor his face wasted: hence a smooth, serene, gently smiling face.
